ledger.problem: decoded the (t,c) tile with torch unconditionally at the top of the tile loop, although the fused Triton updater and the kernel grad_x path never read it
ledger.evidence: update-disabled ablation for counter_triton: 15.44 ms/step while the update was 20.49 ms; the decode produced ~13 torch kernels per layer per step
ledger.change: decode lazily: only the torch grad_x fallback and the torch update fallback request (t,c); fused paths skip it

ledger.problem: built torch.tensor([seed], device=...) per call: a pageable H2D copy that synchronizes the stream, once per layer per step
ledger.evidence: torch.profiler showed cudaStreamSynchronize x360 (24/step) and cudaMemcpyAsync in the counter_triton step
ledger.change: cache one int64 seed slot per device and fill_ it (async device store)

ledger.problem: the char-LM gate only forwarded counter kwargs to the pure-torch kinds ('counter','counter_rms'); the fused kinds existed but could not be selected with the right lr/C, so the published 80-86k baseline measured the torch reference path
ledger.change: forward counter kwargs to counter_packed/counter_triton/counter_fast and add the new kind; use counter_triton for the gate comparison

ledger.problem: lr=0 was not a bit-exact no-op: 2 of 16,777,216 codes at 4096^2 (1 of 4.2M at 2048^2) moved by one quantum, deterministically; torch reference moved none
ledger.change: exact no-op guard: when lr==0 and s_old==s_new return the loaded code unchanged

ledger.problem: no one-launch decoder from packed 6-bit state to a dense fp32 tile existed for the plain format; the torch decode was ~13 kernels
ledger.change: new Triton decode kernel (bitwise-identical to scale*t: decode err 0.0) + cuBLAS matmul + inherited fused update, exposed as kind 'counter_fast'

effect.verdict: bitwise-exact and equal at layer level, but slower at model level (43.5 ms vs 20.6 ms): extra launch + allocation per direction; kept as an alternative, not the recommended path
